findings.text: the fragment says the second cause "surfaced only once the first was repaired", but the run's own logs/base-arm-vanished-bind.log at the same base 00e5bd109e44209141475c852cd5490b8bef9be3 already read 3 failed / 4 passed with both bind-refusal cases failing, so the base arm the manifest calls the negative control (1 failed / 6 passed) is the more favourable of two runs of one revision and the flakiness that motivates the fix is left unstated.

the sleep-5 reproduction "failed in 12.65s" offered as the deterministic evidence for cause 2 exists in no log under the run directory, so the one claim that could show the second cause failing on demand cannot be checked.

the guard for cause 2 is timing-dependent: reinstating `sleep 30` stays green on an unloaded host and only reddens when the child outlives the 30s startup watch, so the regression this line prevents would survive a normal local run.

baseline_suite.failure_ids is the integer 0 while after_suite.failure_ids is [], so a reader parsing the pair as lists gets one that is not, even though both read 58 passed EXIT=0 and the derived added-failure set is empty.
